title: Pinoy recruited for alleged foreign military job intercepted

blocks.text: Bureau of Immigration Building in Intramuros, Manila
MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Immigration has intercepted another Filipino who was allegedly bound for a military job outside the country.

In a statement on November 18, the Bureau of Immigration said it intercepted a man at Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 on November 7 as he attempted to board a flight to Vietnam for a purported job with a foreign military.
According to the bureau, the passenger was flagged for secondary inspection after immigration officers noticed inconsistencies in his travel documents and statements.
During further questioning, the man revealed that he had responded to a Facebook advertisement promising a monthly salary of over P100,000, along with a $10,000 signing bonus.
A foreign recruiter subsequently moved their communications to WhatsApp and covered his airfare and other travel expenses.
The passenger eventually admitted that tourism was not his true purpose for traveling.

After assessing him as a potential victim of human trafficking or illegal recruitment, BI officers turned the passenger over to the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking for further assessment and assistance.
The Bureau of Immigration has also intercepted Filipinos in previous months who were allegedly recruited for military, border guard or armed conflict zone jobs.
All cases involved the same scheme, which offered a signing bonus in foreign currency and a six-digit monthly salary in pesos.
